hindi: श्रीगणेश को नमस्कार।
english: Salutation to the revered Gaṇeśa.
notes:
The leading '||' is a printed mark, kept as a token.

words.gloss: fruits of madana (emetic nut, Randia spinosa; standard), jīmūtaka (Luffa echinata, bandal; probable), ikṣvāku (a bitter bottle-gourd, Lagenaria siceraria; disputed, and the reading is conjectural here), kukkṛtikā (unidentified), śātakī (unidentified) and kuṭaja (kurchi, Holarrhena pubescens; standard) (drug names)

english: Among the substances for emesis, the fruits of madana (emetic nut), jīmūtaka, ikṣvāku, kukkṛtikā, śātakī and kuṭaja (kurchi) are the best.

english: And the precedence among these, and among these preparations, is according to doṣa, dūṣya (what is vitiated) and the like.

text_flags.why: 'dṛṣya' is probably 'dūṣya' (that which is vitiated)
proofread pass (metre, error): दृष्य should be दूष्य

lines_iast: doṣādīnāmeva cātibahuvasthābhedādvamanādiṣu kalyānāṃ vyāpadāṃ sādhanānāṃ ca yadasaṃkhyeyatvaṃ

words.gloss: from the very many differences of state

hindi: और दोष आदि की ही अत्यन्त बहुत अवस्थाओं के भेद से वमन आदि में कल्पों, व्यापदों और साधनों की जो असंख्यता है।
english: And because of the very many different states of doṣa and the rest, the formulations, mishaps and means in emesis and the like are innumerable.

text_flags.why: 'kalyāna' does not fit; 'kalpa' (formulations) is the sense and matches the chapter's theme
u+a would normally become 'va' (bahv-avasthā); possible misprint

notes:
'yad asaṃkhyeyatvam' is rendered as a statement ('...are innumerable'); the sentence continues in the next unit with 'ataḥ' (therefore).
OPEN (05.01.7) [minor] english / "the very many different states of doṣa and the rest": eva (doṣādīnām eva) is dropped in English (Hindi keeps "ही") Suggested: add "alone/just" or note it; e.g. "of doṣa and the rest alone"

words.gloss: for the purpose of showing the path of variations

hindi: इसलिए बुद्धिमानों को विकल्प के मार्ग का दर्शन कराने के लिए केवल उदाहरण के रूप में कल्पसिद्धिस्थान का उपदेश किया जाएगा।
english: Therefore, in order to show the intelligent the path of variations, the Kalpasiddhi section is taught as a mere example.
notes: 'mātra' taken as 'merely'. 'kalpasiddhisthāna' is the name of the section (Kalpa and Siddhi).

lines_deva: अथ वसन्तग्रीष्मयोरन्तरे प्रशस्तेऽहनि मुहूर्त्ते च नातिहरितपांडूनि मदनफलान्याददीत
lines_iast: atha vasantagrīṣmayorantare praśaste'hani muhūrtte ca nātiharitapāṃḍūni madanaphalānyādadīta

words.gram: loc. sg. (n. with ahani; m. if also with muhūrte)

words.gloss: madana fruits (emetic nut; plant identified in line 05.01.4)

hindi: फिर वसन्त और ग्रीष्म के बीच, शुभ दिन और शुभ मुहूर्त में, न बहुत हरे और न बहुत पीले मदन यानी मैनफल के फलों को ग्रहण करे।
english: Then, in the interval between spring and summer, on an auspicious day and at an auspicious moment, one should take madana (emetic nut) fruits that are neither very green nor very pale.
notes:
'muhūrtte' is a variant spelling of muhūrte. 'harita-pāṇḍu' read as 'green and pale-yellow'; as a single compound it could mean 'green-pale'. praśaste may qualify only ahani, or both ahani and muhūrte; both translations take it with both.
OPEN (05.01.9) [minor] hindi / पीले: pāṇḍu is "pale" (yellowish-white); Hindi "पीले" (yellow) vs English "pale" are inconsistent (same in line 05.01.35) Suggested: use one rendering for pāṇḍu in both languages (see glossary_suggestions)

lines_iast: tāni pramṛjya kuśamūḍake badhvā gomayenālipya yavabusamāṣaśālivrīhikulatthamudgānyatamarāśāvaṣṭarātramuṣitānyuddhṛtyātape śoṣayet

words.gloss: in a bundle (mūḍaka) of kuśa grass (Desmostachya bipinnata; standard)

in a heap of any one of: yava (barley, Hordeum vulgare; standard), husk (busa), māṣa (black gram, Vigna mungo; standard), śāli (winter rice, Oryza sativa; standard), vrīhi (rice, Oryza sativa, the ordinary rice grain; standard), kulattha (horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum; standard), mudga (green gram, Vigna radiata; standard)

hindi: उन्हें पोंछकर, कुश के मूढक में बाँधकर, गोबर से लीपकर, यव यानी जौ, बुस, माष यानी उड़द, शालि यानी अगहनी धान, व्रीहि यानी धान, कुलत्थ यानी कुलथी या मुद्ग यानी मूँग में से किसी एक की राशि में आठ रात रखे हुए को निकालकर धूप में सुखाए।
english: Having wiped them, tied them in a bundle of kuśa grass and smeared it with cow-dung, and (having kept them) for eight nights in a heap of any one of yava (barley), husk (busa), māṣa (black gram), śāli (winter rice), vrīhi (rice), kulattha (horse gram) or mudga (green gram), one should take them out and dry them in the sun.

text_flags.why: absolutive of √bandh normally has the doubled dh; possible misprint

notes:
'mūḍaka' is taken as 'bundle' (compare Marathi mūḍh); uncertain. 'busa' read as husk/chaff, 'yava-busa' could also be read as 'barley-husk'. Grain names are kept as names. The packet (smeared with cow-dung) is taken as the thing kept in the heap; the Sanskrit does not state this.
OPEN (05.01.10) [minor] english / "smeared it with cow-dung": "it" (the bundle) is an inference; Sanskrit object is tāni (the fruits); note already admits this Suggested: avoid "it" or keep note; low priority

lines_deva: सुशुष्काणां पिप्पलीरुद्धृत्य दधिघृतमधुपललविमृदिताः पुनः शोषयित्वा नवं कलशमरजस्कमाकंठं पूरयित्वा सुगुप्तं निधापयेत्
lines_iast: suśuṣkāṇāṃ pippalīruddhṛtya dadhighṛtamadhupalalavimṛditāḥ punaḥ śoṣayitvā navaṃ kalaśamarajaskamākaṃṭhaṃ pūrayitvā suguptaṃ nidhāpayet

words.gloss: pippalī (drug name; the bare word usually means long pepper, Piper longum, standard for that word; in this madana chapter 'phalapippalī' probably means the dried madana fruit pieces, probable, see notes)
rubbed with curd, ghee, honey and palala

hindi: भली-भाँति सूखे हुओं में से पिप्पलियों को निकालकर, दही, घी, शहद और पलल में मसली हुई उन्हें फिर सुखाकर, नए और धूल-रहित कलश को गले तक भरकर, उसे अच्छी तरह सुरक्षित रखवाए।
english: From the well-dried ones, having taken out the pippalīs, rubbed with curd, ghee, honey and palala, and dried them again, one should fill a new, dust-free pot up to the neck and have it stored well guarded.
notes: 'pippalī' is not glossed beyond the name here (it is the thing drawn out of the dried fruits; the identity is not stated). 'palala' literally paste (also flesh/sesame paste in dictionaries); kept as a name. The pot is understood to be filled with the rubbed pippalīs. Identification: bare 'pippalī' is long pepper (Piper longum; standard). Here, in the chapter on madana, the 'pippalīs' drawn out of the dried fruits and called 'phalapippalī' in the next units are probably the dried madana fruit pieces themselves (read from the context: the pieces are drawn out of the dried madana fruits, are later called phalapippalī, and are kept apart from the kernel, majjā; not checked against a commentary; probable, not certain), so 'long pepper' is not put in the translation. 'palala' is ground sesame paste in some references (kept as the name palala).

lines_deva: ततः प्रयोगकाले तासां फलपिप्पलीनामंतर्मुखमुष्टिं यावद्वा साधु मन्येत जर्जरीकृत्य यष्टीमधुककोविदारकर्बुदारनीपविदुलबिंबीशणपुष्पीसदापुष्पीप्रत्यक्पुष्प्यन्यतमकषाये वा रात्रिमुषितं विमृदितं पूतं सूत्रोक्तविधिना पाययेत्
lines_iast: tataḥ prayogakāle tāsāṃ phalapippalīnāmaṃtarmukhamuṣṭiṃ yāvadvā sādhu manyeta jarjarīkṛtya yaṣṭīmadhukakovidārakarbudāranīpavidulabiṃbīśaṇapuṣpīsadāpuṣpīpratyakpuṣpyanyatamakaṣāye vā rātrimuṣitaṃ vimṛditaṃ pūtaṃ sūtroktavidhinā pāyayet

words.gloss: of the fruit-pippalīs (here probably the dried madana fruit pieces, as in line 05.01.11; probable)
a fist with the mouth inward (a handful)

in the decoction of any one of yaṣṭīmadhuka (liquorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra; standard), kovidāra (orchid tree, Bauhinia variegata; probable, since the name is also applied to Bauhinia purpurea), karbudāra (a Bauhinia, perhaps the white-flowered kovidāra or Bauhinia purpurea; disputed), nīpa (kadamba, Neolamarckia cadamba; probable), vidula (cane, Calamus rotang, or a willow, Salix; disputed), bimbī (ivy gourd, Coccinia grandis; standard), śaṇapuṣpī (a Crotalaria species of the sunn-hemp type; disputed), sadāpuṣpī (possibly a name of arka, Calotropis gigantea; disputed), pratyakpuṣpī (prickly chaff-flower, Achyranthes aspera; standard) (drug names)
by the method stated in the Sūtra (section)

hindi: तब प्रयोग के समय उन फल-पिप्पलियों की भीतर की ओर मुँह वाली एक मुट्ठी, अथवा जितनी ठीक समझे, कूटकर यष्टीमधुक यानी मुलेठी, कोविदार यानी कचनार, कर्बुदार, नीप यानी कदम्ब, विदुल, बिम्बी यानी कुन्दरू, शणपुष्पी, सदापुष्पी या प्रत्यक्पुष्पी यानी चिरचिटा में से किसी एक के कषाय में, अथवा रात भर रखे, मसले और छाने हुए को सूत्रस्थान में कही विधि से पिलाए।
english: Then, at the time of use, one should coarsely crush a fist (with the mouth inward) of those fruit-pippalīs, or as much as one thinks fit, and, in the decoction of any one of yaṣṭīmadhuka (liquorice), kovidāra (orchid tree), karbudāra, nīpa (kadamba), vidula, bimbī (ivy gourd), śaṇapuṣpī, sadāpuṣpī or pratyakpuṣpī (prickly chaff-flower), or else kept for a night, rubbed and strained, have it drunk by the method stated in the Sūtra section.
notes:
'antarmukhamuṣṭim' (a fist with the mouth inward) is uncertain: it may be a handful measure; the printed sense is kept. The second 'vā' after 'kaṣāye' is ambiguous (alternative way of taking it); rendered as 'or else'. All names are drug names; identifications are in the word gloss (owner policy 2026-10-17). 'Sūtra' is taken as the Sūtrasthāna.
OPEN (05.01.12) [error] gloss / karbudāra 'Bauhinia purpurea; probable': Overconfident: karbudāra is commonly explained as a white-flowered form of kovidāra; B. purpurea is only one candidate. Should be disputed (applied in the same patch as the kovidāra tag). Suggested: tag disputed

words.gloss: in phlegm (kapha), fever, gulma (abdominal lump), pratiśyāya (coryza, running cold) and internal abscesses (antar-vidradhi)

hindi: कफ, ज्वर, गुल्म यानी पेट के भीतर की गाँठ, प्रतिश्याय यानी जुकाम और भीतरी विद्रधि यानी भीतरी फोड़े में विशेष रूप से, फिर पित्त के आने तक।
english: Especially in phlegm (śleṣma), fever, gulma (abdominal lump), pratiśyāya (coryza, common cold) and internal abscesses, again until Pitta comes.
notes: Continues the sentence of the previous unit. 'śleṣmajvara' could also be read as 'kapha-fever'; 'punar ā-pitta-gamanāt' is obscure ('repeatedly until pitta comes up'?); translated closely with a supplied verb in Hindi.

hindi: उससे भली प्रकार वमन होता है।
english: By that one vomits well.

lines_deva: फलपिप्पलीचूर्णं वा स्वक्वाथभावितं त्रिभागत्विफलाचूर्णं कोविदारादिनिर्यूहेण बलवत्कफप्रसेकापच्यर्बुदग्रंथिज्वरोदरा रोचकेषु पिबेत्
lines_iast: phalapippalīcūrṇaṃ vā svakvāthabhāvitaṃ tribhāgatviphalācūrṇaṃ kovidārādiniryūheṇa balavatkaphaprasekāpacyarbudagraṃthijvarodarā rocakeṣu pibet

words.gloss: powder of triphalā (three-fruit group: harītakī, Terminalia chebula; bibhītaka, Terminalia bellirica; āmalakī, Phyllanthus emblica; standard) in three parts
with the decoction of kovidāra and the rest

strong kapha, praseka (flow, trickling; in clinical use excessive salivation), apaci (chain of glandular swellings, cervical lymphadenitis / scrofula; probable), arbuda (tumour, growth), granthi (nodular swelling, cyst), fever, udara (belly)
in loss of relish for food

hindi: अथवा अपने क्वाथ में भावित फल-पिप्पली का चूर्ण, तीन भाग त्रिफला यानी हरड़, बहेड़ा और आँवला के चूर्ण के साथ, कोविदार आदि के क्वाथ से, प्रबल कफ, प्रसेक यानी मुँह में पानी भर आना, अपची यानी गण्डमाला, अर्बुद यानी ट्यूमर, ग्रन्थि यानी गाँठ, ज्वर, उदर और अरुचि में पिए।
english: Or the powder of fruit-pippalī steeped in its own decoction, with triphalā (harītakī, bibhītaka and āmalakī: the three myrobalans) powder in three parts, one should drink with a decoction of kovidāra and the rest, in strong Kapha, praseka (excessive salivation), apaci (glandular swellings of the neck), arbuda (tumour), granthi (nodular swelling, cyst), fever, udara and arocaka (loss of relish for food).

text_flags.why: 'tviphalā' is a misprint for 'triphalā'

notes:
The printed line breaks the word 'jvarodarā rocakeṣu': the space splits 'udara-arocakeṣu' in the middle of a sandhi (a+a=ā). The first token is given 'udara-' and the second 'arocakeṣu'. 'balavat' may qualify only 'kapha' or all the conditions. 'tribhāga' could also mean 'a third part'. Modern equivalents: udara in a list of diseases usually means udara roga (disease of the belly, such as abdominal enlargement); the translation keeps 'belly' as decided. Triphalā members are standard (harītakī, bibhītaka, āmalakī). The 'kovidāra and the rest' group (kovidārādi) is not enumerated here.
OPEN (05.01.15) [minor] gloss / praseka ("flow (of saliva)"): "of saliva" is an added specific; plain literal sense is "flow, trickling" Suggested: see glossary_suggestions; English/Hindi keep praseka as a term

words.gloss: powder of the kernel of the madana fruit
with the decoction of jīmūtaka and the rest
gone to the seat of kapha

hindi: अथवा मदनफल यानी मैनफल की मज्जा का चूर्ण जीमूतक आदि के क्वाथ से, जब पित्त कफ के स्थान में गया हो।
english: Or the powder of the kernel of the madana (emetic nut) fruit, with a decoction of jīmūtaka and the rest, when Pitta has gone to the seat of Kapha.
notes: 'majjā' taken as the inner kernel (literally marrow). No verb in the unit; the sentence is elliptical.

lines_deva: मदनफलमज्जसिद्धं वा पयस्तस्मिन्वा यवागूमधोभागे रक्तपित्ते हृद्दाहे च
lines_iast: madanaphalamajjasiddhaṃ vā payastasminvā yavāgūmadhobhāge raktapitte hṛddāhe ca

words.gloss: cooked with the kernel of the madana fruit
in raktapitta (blood-pitta; a bleeding disorder, bleeding from the upper or lower passages)

hindi: अथवा मदनफल यानी मैनफल की मज्जा से सिद्ध किया दूध, या उसी में यवागू, निचले भाग में रक्तपित्त यानी रक्तस्राव के रोग में और हृदय की जलन में।
english: Or milk cooked with the kernel of the madana (emetic nut) fruit, or a gruel (yavāgū) in that, in raktapitta (a bleeding disorder) in the lower part and in burning of the heart (heartburn).
notes: 'adhobhāge' may mean 'in the lower part (of the body)' going with raktapitta, or 'in the lower portion (of the milk/preparation)'; the former is rendered. 'majja' is read as a variant of 'majjā'.

lines_deva: तस्य वा पयसः शीतस्य संतानिकांऽजलिं पित्ते प्रकुपिते उरःकंठहृदये च तनुकफोपादिग्धे
lines_iast: tasya vā payasaḥ śītasya saṃtānikāṃ'jaliṃ pitte prakupite uraḥkaṃṭhahṛdaye ca tanukaphopādigdhe

words.gloss: santānikā (the film/skin that forms on milk)
when the chest, throat and heart

hindi: अथवा उस ठंडे दूध की संतानिका यानी मलाई की एक अञ्जलि, जब पित्त कुपित हो और छाती, कंठ तथा हृदय पतले कफ से लिप्त हों।
english: Or a palmful of the santānikā (skin, milk-cream) of that cold milk, when Pitta is aggravated and the chest, throat and heart are smeared with thin Kapha.
notes: 'santānikā' is taken as the film that forms on milk. 'uraḥkaṇṭhahṛdaye' is read as a dvandva in the locative, agreeing with 'upādigdhe'.

hindi: अथवा फल आदि के क्वाथ से इक्कीस बार भली-भाँति भावित फल-पिप्पलियों को पुष्प के पराग के समान चूर्ण से चूर्णित करे। संध्या के समय सरोवर में बड़े कमल में रखकर रात भर रखे उसे प्रातः फिर चूर्ण मिलाकर निकाल ले। हरिद्रा यानी हल्दी, कृसरा यानी खिचड़ी, दूध या यवागू में से किसी एक को सेंधा नमक, गुड़ और फाणित यानी राब मिलाकर गले तक पीकर, सूँघता हुआ, सुकुमार, उचित गन्ध की सम्पदा से जिसके कफ और पित्त उभर आए हों और जो औषध से द्वेष रखता हो, वह इस प्रकार सुख से वमन करता है।
english: Or the fruit-pippalīs, well steeped twenty-one times in a decoction of phala and the rest, one should dust over with a powder like flower pollen; in the evening, in a lake, a large lotus; that kept for a night, and in the morning taken out and powdered again; having drunk up to the neck any one of haridrā (turmeric), kṛsarā (a rice-and-pulse dish, khichdi), milk or gruel, with rock salt, jaggery and phāṇita (thick cane-juice syrup) added, smelling, a delicate person, whose Kapha and Pitta are stirred by a fitting abundance of fragrance and who hates medicine, thus vomits easily.

english: There: in flowers, milk; in fruits that are hairy, a thin gruel (peyā); in the remaining fruits, santānikā (milk-cream); in those without hair, curd or the upper part of the curd.

text_flags.why: 'loma-lomavat' looks like a doubled syllable; possible misprint for 'lomavatsu' (hairy)

hindi: पके हुए, पुराने अथवा सूखे जीमूतक यानी देवदाली के फलों का चूर्ण वातपित्त में।
english: The powder of the ripe, old, or dried fruits of jīmūtaka (bitter luffa), in vātapitta.

Identification (probable): jīmūtaka = Luffa echinata Roxb. (bitter luffa; Hindi devadālī, bandāl). Some lists treat other Luffa species under this name; the unit does not say which.

english: Two or three (of them), crushed, steeped in the decoction of any one of the fresh ones beginning with āragvadha (golden shower tree) or of paṭolī (pointed gourd), and churned, in fever (jvara) born of Pitta and phlegm.

hindi: जीमूतक यानी देवदाली का चूर्ण अथवा कल्क ठंडे जल के साथ, पित्त से उत्पन्न में। वही गरम जल के साथ, वात और कफ से उत्पन्न में अथवा कफ से उत्पन्न में।
english: Jīmūtaka powder or paste with cold water, in what is born of Pitta. That same, with warm (water), in what is born of Vāta and Kapha, or of Kapha.

line 05.01.39: The noun for 'what is born of Pitta' (probably jvara, as in line 05.01.38) is not stated.
line 05.01.40: 'water' is understood from the previous unit.

words.gloss: of jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, ikṣu (sugarcane, Saccharum officinarum; standard) and śatāvarī (Asparagus racemosus; standard); jīvaka and ṛṣabhaka are disputed (usually Malaxis acuminata and M. muscifera, rare orchids, often replaced by substitutes in practice)

hindi: जीवक, ऋषभक, इक्षु यानी गन्ना और शतावरी में से किसी एक के स्वरस के साथ, पित्त से उत्पन्न में।
english: With the expressed juice of any one of jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, ikṣu (sugarcane) and śatāvarī (wild asparagus), in what is born of Pitta.
notes: Genitive plural followed by genitive singular anyatamasya ('of any one of them'). ikṣu is kept as a name. Identifications: ikṣu = Saccharum officinarum L., sugarcane (standard); śatāvarī = Asparagus racemosus Willd. (standard); jīvaka = Malaxis acuminata D.Don and ṛṣabhaka = Malaxis muscifera (Lindl.) Kuntze (both disputed; the true drugs are rare and substitutes are used). Jīvaka and ṛṣabhaka also belong to the jīvanīya group (see line 05.01.61).

hindi: अथवा पहले की भाँति पकाया हुआ घृत।
english: Or ghee cooked as before.
notes: 'As before' refers back to an earlier preparation; not named here.

in kāsa (cough), śvāsa (breath-trouble; dyspnoea, asthma-type), jvara (fever), chardi (vomiting), viṣa (poison) and phlegm-ailments

english: Ikṣvāku (bitter bottle gourd), however, is especially to be applied in kāsa (cough), śvāsa (breath-trouble; dyspnoea), jvara (fever), chardi (vomiting), viṣa (poison) and phlegm-ailments.

(tikta-alābu); the text does not say bitter. Disease equivalents (standard): kāsa = cough; śvāsa = breathlessness/dyspnoea (includes asthma-type illness); jvara = fever; chardi = vomiting.

english: Milk boiled with the sprouts of that one while it is without flower and fruit, in one whose Pitta is excessive and in fever of Pitta and Kapha; but in the case of the flowers and the rest, the applications are like those of rāta-jīmūta.

in kapha-pīnasa (Kapha-type pīnasa: chronic nasal catarrh, rhinitis; standard)

english: Or the patient, desiring emesis, should drink the expressed juice of the ikṣvāku fruit prepared in threefold milk, in Pitta, in kapha-pīnasa (chronic nasal catarrh) and in svarasāda (hoarseness, loss of voice).
notes: triguṇa-kṣīra: 'milk three times (the quantity)' is the plain sense; the exact measure is not stated. pibeta is a middle-voice optative, kept as printed.

notes: Modern equivalents (standard): gulma = abdominal lump; galagaṇḍa = goitre; granthi = nodular swelling; arbuda = tumour; ślīpada = filariasis (elephantiasis); udara here is an ailment term, not just 'belly'.

lines_deva: ततस्तस्मिंस्त्रिभागघृते घृतसमानि पिष्ट्वा तुंबीबीजानि तदर्द्धाशिकानि च प्रत्येकं जीमुतमहाजालिनीवत्सककृतवेधनानि क्वाथतुल्यमेव च त्रिकटुकमावपेत्

english: Then, into that, in which the ghee is a third part, one should add tumbī (bottle gourd) seeds ground equal to the ghee, and, each at half that portion, jīmūta, mahājālinī, vatsaka (kuṭaja) and kṛtavedhana, and trikaṭuka (dry ginger, long pepper and black pepper) equal to the decoction.

Wall. ex G.Don = H. antidysenterica (probable; indrayava is its seed). kṛtavedhana = koṣātakī, Luffa acutangula (L.) Roxb. (probable; some lists give Luffa cylindrica). jīmūta presumably = jīmūtaka (see line 05.01.37). mahājālinī: unidentified (no identification is relied on here).

lines_iast: tamavalihya pramadhyāmanupibettadvaddhameva ca kalpaḥ kāśmaryādiṣu caturṣu mahāpañcamūlāṃgeṣu pṛthakpṛthagukto veditavyaḥ

words.gloss: in those beginning with kāśmarya (kāśmarya = Gmelina arborea, gambhārī; standard)
in the members of the great five roots

english: Having licked it, one should drink a pramathyā afterwards, and likewise ghee; the procedure (kalpa) is to be understood as stated separately in each of the four members of the great five roots, beginning with kāśmarya.

The text does not list them here. Bilva was dealt with in line 05.01.56, so the 'four' are presumably the other four; this is an inference, not stated in the text. kāśmarya = Gmelina arborea Roxb. (standard).

words.gloss: dhāmārgava (a Luffa species; disputed whether Luffa cylindrica, sponge gourd, or L. acutangula)
in gara (concocted poison), gulma (abdominal lump), udara (belly-ailment), kāsa (cough) and ailments arising from accumulation of Kapha
located in the seat of phlegm

hindi: धामार्गव विशेष रूप से गर यानी बनाया हुआ विष, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ, उदर यानी पेट के रोग, कास यानी खाँसी तथा कफ के संचय से उत्पन्न रोगों में, जो स्थिर और भारी हों उनमें, कफ के आशय में स्थित रोगों में, और कण्ठ में आश्रय वाले वात-कफ में।
english: Dhāmārgava, especially in gara (concocted poison), gulma (abdominal lump), udara (belly-ailment), kāsa (cough) and the ailments arising from an accumulation of Kapha; in those that are firm and heavy, in those located in the seat of phlegm, and in Vāta-phlegm whose seat is the throat.

text_flags.why: anusvāra after dhā is probably an error (dhāmārgava in lines 05.01.62-64)

notes: sthireṣu and guruṣu are taken to qualify the ailments (rogeṣu). The end of the unit has no verb of application. Scope of -uttha-roga: translated as applying only to kapha-saṃcaya; it could govern all preceding members (ailments arising from gara, gulma, udara, kāsa and Kapha accumulation). Identification (disputed): dhāmārgava is a Luffa species (Cucurbitaceae); lists give Luffa cylindrica (L.) M.Roem. (sponge gourd) or Luffa acutangula (L.) Roxb., and it is sometimes confused with kṛtavedhana/koṣātakī. Not resolved here; Hindi keeps the Sanskrit name.

words.gloss: joined with powder of any one of the jīvanīya group (members in notes)

hindi: जीवनीय गण में से किसी एक के चूर्ण से युक्त, मधु और शर्करा सहित, उन्हीं के काढ़ों से लेह तैयार करके, पित्त के गौण होने पर कफ की अवस्था में विधान करे।
english: Having prepared lehas (licked preparations) joined with the powder of any one of the jīvanīya (life-promoting) group, with honey and sugar, and made with decoctions of those, one should prescribe them in the phlegm condition in which Pitta is secondary.
notes:
tat-kaṣāyaiḥ: 'their decoctions' is taken as the decoctions of the drugs just named. upasarjana literally 'accompaniment, subordinate'. Group (standard, from Caraka's jīvanīya list; the Aṣṭāṅga Saṅgraha list is expected to agree but was not checked here): jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, medā, mahāmedā, kākolī, kṣīrakākolī, mudgaparṇī, māṣaparṇī, jīvantī, madhuka (licorice root). Several of these (jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, medā, kākolī) are rare or disputed drugs.

english: Dhāmārgava paste with a broth of tumbaru and dhānya, in poisons.

(= Z. alatum; Hindi tejbal, timur). dhānya: literally 'grain'; some lists read dhānyaka, coriander (disputed). The earlier sense note (kept as a name in the translation) is not changed.

words.gloss: kāsamarda (Senna occidentalis, coffee senna; disputed, some give Senna sophera)

hindi: सुमनः, सौमनस्या, यवानी यानी अजवायन, हरिद्रा यानी हल्दी, चोरक, हैमवती, महासहा, क्षुद्रसहा, वृश्चीव, अर्बी के बीज, पुनर्नवा और कासमर्द में से किसी एक के काढ़े के साथ, अथवा एक या दो धामार्गव, मन के विकारों में।
english: With the decoction of any one of sumanas, saumanasyā, yavānī (ajwain), haridrā (turmeric), coraka, haimavatī, mahāsahā, kṣudrasahā, vṛścīva, arbī seeds, punarnavā (hogweed) and kāsamarda, or one or two of dhāmārgava, in disorders of the mind.
notes:
Doubtful: the split of the long compound (especially vṛścīva-arbī-bīja: sandhi a+a, but arbī is unknown, so the member may be damaged or the division different, e.g. vṛścī + vārbī) and saumanasyā as a drug name. 'one or two' dhāmārgava: the thing counted is not stated (fruit, part?). All names kept untranslated. Alternative syntax: dhāmārgavam (one or two) may be the main item used with the decoction of any one of the listed drugs, not a separate alternative. Unit left at low confidence: only the surest names were identified (yavānī, haridrā, punarnavā standard; kāsamarda disputed). The other names (sumanas, saumanasyā, coraka, haimavatī, mahāsahā, kṣudrasahā, vṛścīva, arbī) are not identified here because the split of the compound is itself doubtful.

english: Ghee produced from milk cooked with the root of dhāmārgava, or ghee cooked with the six beginning with phala, in disorders of the mind.

in gara (concocted poison), udara (belly-ailment), gulma (abdominal lump), plīha (spleen; splenic enlargement), pale-ailments (pāṇḍu-roga; anaemia) and swelling (śvayathu; oedema)

hindi: कृतवेधन, अत्यन्त कटु, तीक्ष्ण और उष्ण, विशेष रूप से गर, उदर, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ, प्लीहा यानी तिल्ली, पाण्डु रोग यानी रक्ताल्पता और श्वयथु यानी सूजन में तैयार करे।
english: One should prepare kṛtavedhana, exceedingly pungent, sharp and hot, especially for gara, udara, gulma (abdominal lump), plīha (spleen), pale-ailments (pāṇḍu-roga, anaemia) and swelling (śvayathu, oedema).
notes: kalpayet 'should prepare, arrange' (for use). kaṭu = pungent, acrid.

words.gloss: fruit of kuṭaja (Holarrhena pubescens = H. antidysenterica, Hindi kuṛā; standard; its seeds are indrayava)
in those in whom blood, Pitta and Kapha are prominent
in vātaśoṇita (= vātarakta; gout-type disease), visarpa (erysipelas, a spreading skin infection), jvara (fever), kuṣṭha (skin diseases, including leprosy) and the rest

hindi: कुटज यानी कुड़ा का फल, दूसरी ओर, सुकुमार व्यक्तियों में, जिनमें रक्त, पित्त और कफ प्रबल हों उनमें, और वातशोणित यानी वातरक्त, विसर्प यानी फैलने वाला त्वचा का संक्रमण, ज्वर यानी बुखार, कुष्ठ यानी कोढ़ समेत त्वचा के रोग आदि में प्रयोग करे।
english: One should apply kuṭaja (kurchi) fruit, on the other hand, in delicate persons, in those in whom blood, Pitta and Kapha are prominent, and in vātaśoṇita (gout), visarpa (erysipelas), jvara (fever), kuṣṭha (skin diseases, including leprosy) and the rest.

with the decoction of any one of the madanaphala (Randia dumetorum; standard), jīmūtaka, ikṣvāku, jīvantī (Leptadenia reticulata; probable) and jīvaka roots

short u and extra anusvāra: mūla + anyatama gives mūlānyatama

(standard; Hindi āk, madār); madanaphala = Randia dumetorum (Retz.) Poir. (standard; Hindi mainphal); madhūka = Madhuca longifolia (J.Koenig) J.F.Macbr. (probable); kṛśarā = a cooked dish, in the tradition of rice and pulses with sesame (probable), not changed in the translation.
